newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger but underperform.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger but underperform.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in light trade on Wednesday but underperformed their U.S. counterparts with the market boosted by a rebound in U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.
"We were dragged up with the U.S. There was a very good auction in the U.S.," said one Toronto-based bond trader. "That's sort of put a bid to the market."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.10 to C$115.30 to yield 6.752. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 34 basis points from 32 basis points at Tuesday's close.

Canadian and U.S. bonds were weaker this morning after the U.S. dollar was hurt by a report showing that the U.S. trade deficit widened in September. However, Treasuries rebounded following the U.S. five-year auction, pulling the Canadian market with it.

Canada's own five-year bond auction "went moderately well," the trader said. The auction of C$2.7 billion of 7.0 percent bonds due September 1, 2001 had an average yield of 5.273 percent and an average price of C$107.157.
In Canadian economic news, Canada's merchandise trade surplus fell in September to C$3.23 billion from C$3.73 billion in August (revised from C$4.02 billion), Statistics Canada said this morning.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.10 to C$106.47 to yield 6.126 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.13 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to almost zero from two basis points at Tuesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.85 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.16 percent.
